newsitem.title: ITALY: ITALY'S CONSOB FOR MORE FINANCIAL SECTOR AUTONOMY.
newsitem.headline: ITALY'S CONSOB FOR MORE FINANCIAL SECTOR AUTONOMY.

text.p: Italian security houses, banks and investment funds will get more autonomy and responsibility for self-regulation under new draft rules for the financial services sector drawn up by bourse regulator Consob.
The document, drawn up by the watchdog body chaired by Tommaso Padoa Schioppa, has been sent to the relevant financial services' associations for their views, a Consob statement said.
The new measures aim to slim down and streamline current rules governing the financial services sector, giving more freedom to individual operators and their associations to adopt internal rules.
The moves follows Italy's adoption last year of a European Union directive aimed at liberalising the sector.

Consob will retain its supervisory and regulatory role, but it has proposed several changes to existing regulations, including giving operators more autonomy to register orders and investment operations.

However, financial service brokers will have give clearer information to clients about the risks of investment, record on tape all orders taken by telephone and register client complaints for reply with 90 days.
Consob will re-examine the draft measures in September after receiving comments and opinions from market operators.
